strategy.bottleneck: gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel (16.3% of forward) is instruction/ALU bound, not memory bound: runtime integer div/mod on CPG/TP plus scalar loads burn ~185 warp-instructions per 32 outputs; gn_stats_kernel has a 64-bit division in its inner loop.
strategy.optimisation method: Specialize the custom kernels for the fixed C=256/G=32/CPG=8 geometry: replace all runtime integer division/modulo with compile-time shifts and masks, widen the NHWC reads to float4, retile gn_silu_res_nchw to TP=128 with a conflict-free padded shared transpose.
strategy.modification plan:
1. In ModelNew.forward keep the existing PyTorch fallback and additionally route to it unless (C==256 && G==32 && dtype==float32); all new kernels may then assume CPG=8, C=256, C4=64 as compile-time constants. HW stays a runtime argument (shapes 8192 / 4096 / 65536 / 17161 must all work).
2. Rewrite gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel with `constexpr int CPG=8; constexpr int TPX=128;` and 256 threads. Shared array `__shared__ float sm[TPX*9];` (row stride 9 floats = 4608 B) laid out as sm[p*9+c].
3. Load phase (no division): `int t=threadIdx.x; int p=t>>1; int j=t&1; int pg=p0+p;` where `p0 = blockIdx.x*TPX`. If `pg<HW`, do one `float4 v = *reinterpret_cast<const float4*>(x + base + (long long)pg*256 + (j<<2));` and one `float4 gm/bt` load from `gamma + (g<<3) + (j<<2)` / `beta + ...` (both 16-B aligned). Compute `silu((v.k-mu)*rs*gm.k+bt.k)` for k=0..3 and store the 4 scalars to `sm[p*9 + (j<<2) + k]`.
4. `__syncthreads();`
5. Store phase: `for (int k=0;k<4;++k){ int lin=(k<<8)+t; int c=lin>>7; int pl=lin&127; int pg=p0+pl; if(pg<HW){ long long oi=obase+(long long)c*HW+pg; out[oi]=sm[pl*9+c]+res[oi]; } }` — this gives 128 consecutive pixels per channel row (fully coalesced 128-B global segments) and stride-9 shared reads (bank-conflict free).
6. Update the launcher: `grid(( (int)HW + 127)/128, B*G)`, block 256, shared = 128*9*sizeof(float); delete the old TP=32 dynamic-shared path.
7. Build and validate numerics against the reference on all four shapes (this is the compile/correctness milestone).
8. gn_stats_kernel: hardcode `cpg4 = 2`. Change the inner loop to pure 32-bit arithmetic with shifts: `int cnt = (p_end - p_start) << 1; for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < cnt; i += 256) { int p = p_start + (i>>1); int j = i&1; float4 v = *reinterpret_cast<const float4*>(x + base + (long long)p*256 + (j<<2)); ... }`. Remove every `long long` division/modulo (the current `i / cpg4` on a `long long` compiles to a ~50-instruction 64-bit divide). Add `#pragma unroll 4` on this loop for accumulator ILP.
9. gn_silu_nhwc_kernel: replace `idx % C4` with `idx & 63` and `c0 / CPG` with `c0 >> 3`; keep the float4 loads/stores and the same launch shape (it is already at 81% DRAM, this is only instruction cleanup).
10. Anti-regression guards: keep registers/thread <= 40 (check `-Xptxas -v`) so at least 6 blocks/SM remain resident; keep shared/block <= 8 KB; keep every `pg < HW` guard so HW=17161 (odd) and HW=4096 still produce bit-identical results; do not remove the float4 widths anywhere; no in-place writes (out is a fresh at::empty).
11. Re-measure all four shapes; the geometric-mean speedup must not drop on the small (2x256x64x64) or awkward (1x256x131x131) shape.

Ruled out (secondary): occupancy is NOT the limiter for gn_silu_res_nchw - achieved occupancy 88.71%, sm__warps_active 88.87%, eligible warps 3.66/scheduler, no local-memory spilling (0 requests). strategy.bottleneck: 15.2% of steady GPU time (1852 us / 36 launches = ~154 us per forward) is spent in PyTorch TensorIterator `elementwise_kernel` layout copies (x and both 3x3 weights to channels_last) that perform zero math and run far below bandwidth because the NCHW->NHWC permute is uncoalesced on one side.
strategy.optimisation method: Replace the three `.contiguous(memory_format=channels_last)` TensorIterator permutes with custom shared-memory-staged transpose kernels: a per-filter [C,9]->[9,C] transpose for conv1/conv2 weights (fully coalesced both directions), then a 32x32 tiled NCHW->NHWC transpose for x. Pure data movement, bit-identical results.
strategy.modification plan:
1. In _SRC add `__global__ void weight_nchw_to_nhwc_kernel(const float* __restrict__ src, float* __restrict__ dst, int C, int KK)`: grid.x = O (one block per output filter), blockDim 256, dynamic `extern __shared__ float sm[]` holding C*KK floats.
2. Kernel body part A (coalesced read): `const long long base=(long long)blockIdx.x*(long long)C*KK; const int N9=C*KK; for(int i=threadIdx.x;i<N9;i+=256){ float v=src[base+i]; int c=(KK==9)?(i/9):(i/KK); int rs=i-c*KK; sm[rs*C+c]=v; }` — consecutive threads read consecutive addresses (128B/warp). Use the `KK==9` branch so the divide becomes a compile-time magic multiply.
3. `__syncthreads();` part B (coalesced write): `for(int i=threadIdx.x;i<N9;i+=256) dst[base+i]=sm[i];` — dst index is exactly NHWC order ((o*KH+r)*KW+s)*C+c.
4. Host wrapper `torch::Tensor weight_to_nhwc(torch::Tensor w)`: require 4D float32 contiguous (NCHW); O=w.size(0),C=w.size(1),KH,KW; `TORCH_CHECK` C*KH*KW*4 <= 48*1024 (2304 floats = 9216B for this task) otherwise return `w.contiguous(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast)`; allocate `at::empty({O,C,KH,KW}, w.options().memory_format(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast))` so cuDNN still sees a channels_last tensor; launch `<<<O,256,C*KH*KW*sizeof(float),stream>>>`; C10_CUDA_KERNEL_LAUNCH_CHECK; return.
5. Declare `weight_to_nhwc` in _CPP and add to `functions=[...]`. In forward replace the w1/w2 lines with `w1 = _ext.weight_to_nhwc(conv1_weight) if conv1_weight.is_contiguous() else conv1_weight.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last)` (same for w2). Keep the generic fallback branch and all existing fixed-geometry GN kernels untouched. COMPILE AND CHECK CORRECTNESS HERE (first milestone).
6. Add `__global__ void nchw_to_nhwc_kernel(const float* __restrict__ src, float* __restrict__ dst, int C, int HW)`: `__shared__ float t[32][33];` blockDim (32,8), grid (ceil(HW/32), C/32, N). Let p0=blockIdx.x*32, c0=blockIdx.y*32, n=blockIdx.z. Read loop `#pragma unroll for(int i=0;i<32;i+=8){ int c=c0+threadIdx.y+i; int p=p0+threadIdx.x; if(p<HW) t[threadIdx.y+i][threadIdx.x]=src[((long long)n*C+c)*HW+p]; }` (coalesced 128B along HW). `__syncthreads();` write loop `for(int i=0;i<32;i+=8){ int p=p0+threadIdx.y+i; if(p<HW) dst[((long long)n*HW+p)*C+c0+threadIdx.x]=t[threadIdx.x][threadIdx.y+i]; }` (coalesced 128B along C; the 33-stride removes bank conflicts).
7. Host wrapper `x_to_nhwc(x)`: only when x is contiguous NCHW float32 and C%32==0 (C=256 here); allocate `at::empty_like(x, x.options().memory_format(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast))`; else fall back to `x.contiguous(memory_format=channels_last)`. Replace `xl = x.contiguous(...)` with this call. Note H*W=17161 is odd, so the `p<HW` guards in both loops are mandatory.
8. Re-verify numerics on all four shapes (8x256x64x128, 2x256x64x64, 4x256x256x256, 1x256x131x131) — the transform is a pure permutation so results must be bitwise identical to the current kernel.
strategy.evidence: nsys steady table: `elementwise_kernel` = 15.2% of per-forward GPU time (1852 us over 36 launches = 3 copies x 12 forwards = ~154 us/forward) doing zero FLOPs; these are exactly the three `.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last)` calls in forward (x, conv1_weight, conv2_weight). The x copy alone has a hard floor of 134 MB / 1.84 TB/s = 73 us, so the two 2.36 MB weight permutes are costing ~30-40 us each versus a ~3 us coalesced floor — their inner dim is 9 floats (36 B), so a warp writing 32 consecutive c values touches 32 distinct 32 B sectors (~8x read amplification). RULED OUT the conv mainloop (58.3%): 2*65536*256*256*9 = 77.3 GFLOP in 297 us = 260 TFLOP/s TF32, i.e. above the 223 TFLOP/s measured SGEMM-TF32 reference, and the allowed GEMM_Rewrite_CUBLASLT_TF32 would need an im2col buffer of 65536x2304x4 = 604 MB (>330 us of extra traffic), so it cannot win — this is why I depart from allowed_methods. RULED OUT gn_silu_res_nchw (10.5%): it already sits at dram_throughput 77.18% of peak with achieved occupancy 88.87%, and the SOL rule for gn_silu_nhwc states it is 'utilizing greater than 80.0% of the available compute or memory performance of this device' (dram 83.13%), so the custom GN kernels are at the bandwidth roof while the copy kernels are not.

strategy.bottleneck: Everything is bandwidth/tensor-core saturated at fp32/TF32 width: the two cuDNN TF32 convs hold 63.4% of steady GPU time, and the glue kernels move fp32 bytes at 72.8-82.9% DRAM. The only remaining lever is halving bytes and doubling tensor-core rate on the conv1 path.
strategy.optimisation method: Run the conv1 half of the pipeline in fp16 (NHWC): emit x and conv1 weights as __half from the existing transform kernels, let cuDNN use fp16 tensor cores (756 vs 378 TFLOPS peak), and read fp16 in gn_stats/gn_silu, writing fp32 for conv2 (kept TF32 for accuracy).
strategy.modification plan:
1. Add `#include <cuda_fp16.h>` to _SRC; keep every existing specialization (compile-time C=256/CPG=8 shift-mask index math, stride-9 padded shared transpose, custom layout kernels) intact.
2. Change `nchw_to_nhwc_kernel` signature to `(const float* x, __half* out, int HW)`; keep the 32x33 float shared tile and both 4-iteration loops; only the store becomes `out[obase + (long long)hw*256 + c0 + cc] = __float2half(t[cc][hh]);` (a warp still writes 32 contiguous halves = 64B = 2 full sectors, so coalescing is preserved).
3. Change `weight_to_nhwc_kernel` to `(const float* w1, const float* w2, __half* d1, float* d2)`: keep the 2304-float shared staging and the `rs*256 + tid` store, but for `blockIdx.y==0` store `__float2half(...)` into d1 and for `blockIdx.y==1` store float into d2 (conv2 weights stay fp32).
4. Add `gn_stats_half_kernel(const __half* x, float* partial, int HW, int S, int BG)`: identical block/grid mapping and warp+shared reduction as `gn_stats_kernel`, but each loop iteration covers ONE pixel: `cnt = p_end - p_start`, `p = p_start + i`, and load all 8 group channels with one 16B `uint4 raw = *reinterpret_cast<const uint4*>(x + base + (long long)p*256);` then convert with 4x `__half22float2` on `reinterpret_cast<const __half2*>(&raw)`, accumulating sum/sq in float. Keep `#pragma unroll 4` on the loop.
5. Add `compute_stats_half(...)` launcher: byte-identical S/BG heuristic and `gn_finalize_kernel` reuse as `compute_stats`, only calling `gn_stats_half_kernel`.

Add `gn_silu_nhwc_h2f_kernel(const __half* x, float* y, gamma, beta, mean, rstd, int HWC4, int G)`: same 1-D idx over HW*C4 (C4=64), same `c0=(idx&63)<<2`, `g=c0>>3` math; load `uint2 raw` (4 halves, 8B) at `x + (off<<2)`, convert via two `__half22float2`, apply `silu_f((v-mu)*rs*gm+bt)`, store one `float4` to y.
7. Export `void nchw_to_nhwc_half(torch::Tensor x, torch::Tensor out_half, int64_t B, int64_t HW)` and `void gn_silu_nhwc_h2f(torch::Tensor x_half, torch::Tensor out_f32, torch::Tensor gamma, torch::Tensor beta, int64_t B, int64_t HW, int64_t C, int64_t G, double eps)`; obtain half pointers via `reinterpret_cast<__half*>(t.data_ptr<at::Half>())`. Update the _CPP prototypes and the `functions=[...]` list. THIS IS THE LAST STEP NEEDED TO COMPILE.

In ModelNew.forward (specialized branch only): allocate `xl = torch.empty((B,C,H,W), dtype=torch.float16, device=x.device, memory_format=torch.channels_last)` and `w1l = torch.empty((256,256,3,3), dtype=torch.float16, ..., memory_format=torch.channels_last)`; keep `w2l` fp32 channels_last. Call `_ext.nchw_to_nhwc_half(xc, xl, B, HW)` and `_ext.weight_to_nhwc(w1c, w2c, w1l, w2l)`.
9. `y = F.conv2d(xl, w1l, None, 1, 1)` (fp16 NHWC, cuDNN fp16 tensor cores, fp32 accumulate); allocate `y32 = torch.empty((B,C,H,W), dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device, memory_format=torch.channels_last)` and call `_ext.gn_silu_nhwc_h2f(y, y32, g1, b1, B, HW, C, G, eps)`.

Leave the rest unchanged: `F.conv2d(y32, w2l, None, 1, 1)` stays fp32/TF32 and `gn_silu_res_nchw` stays fp32 — conv2's output feeds GN2 directly, where an fp16 rounding of a 4-sigma element becomes ~7e-3 after (x-mu)*rstd*gamma and would exceed the 0.0028 tolerance; conv1's fp16 output error is averaged over 2304 taps by conv2 and stays ~1e-3.

strategy.evidence: nsys steady-state: the cuDNN TF32 conv holds 63.4% (7,155us/24 launches) of per-forward GPU time, so it is the only target with >36% Amdahl room; at 77.3 GFLOP per conv and 298us it runs at ~259 TFLOPS, i.e. 69% of the 378 TFLOPS TF32 dense peak — near vendor-optimal for TF32, so no better TF32 tiling exists, but fp16 doubles the peak to 756 TFLOPS. strategy.optimisation method: MultiKernelScheduling: split the batch into 2 independent halves and run the whole per-chunk chain (transform, conv1, GN1+SiLU, conv2, GN2+SiLU+residual) on two CUDA streams with event ordering, so one chunk's DRAM-bound glue overlaps the other chunk's tensor-core conv. Gated to B>=4.
strategy.modification plan:
1. CUDA (_SRC): add ONE new launcher `void gn_silu_res_nchw_into(torch::Tensor x, torch::Tensor res, torch::Tensor gamma, torch::Tensor beta, torch::Tensor out, int64_t B, int64_t HW, int64_t C, int64_t G, double eps)` — body identical to `gn_silu_res_nchw` (same compute_stats call, same grid `dim3(((int)HW+127)/128, B*G)`, 256 threads) except it does NOT `at::empty`; it passes `out.data_ptr<float>()`. Leave `gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel`, the stride-9 shared transpose, the compile-time C=256/CPG=8 shift-mask index math, `nchw_to_nhwc_kernel` and `weight_to_nhwc_kernel` byte-for-byte unchanged.
2. Add its prototype to _CPP and its name to `functions=[...]`.
3. Python: factor the specialized path into a helper `_run_chunk(self, xc_c, w1l, w2l, g1,b1,g2,b2, eps, out_slice, Bc, HW, C, G)` that does exactly today's sequence: allocate `xl` (channels_last, Bc) -> `_ext.nchw_to_nhwc(xc_c, xl, Bc, HW)` -> `F.conv2d(xl, w1l, None,1,1)` -> `_ext.gn_silu_nhwc(...)` -> `F.conv2d(y, w2l, None,1,1)` -> `_ext.gn_silu_res_nchw_into(y, xc_c, g2,b2, out_slice, Bc, HW, C, G, eps)`.
4. In forward (specialized branch): allocate `out = torch.empty(B*C*HW, ...)` once, run `_ext.weight_to_nhwc(w1c,w2c,w1l,w2l)` on the current stream, then call `_run_chunk` ONCE with `xc`, `out` and Bc=B. **THIS IS THE LAST STEP NEEDED TO COMPILE AND MATCH** (behaviour identical to today).
5. Add module-level lazily-created stream cache: `_STREAMS=None`; on first use create `[torch.cuda.Stream(), torch.cuda.Stream()]` (reused across calls, never re-created per forward).
6. Gate: take the 2-stream path only when `B >= 4 and B % 2 == 0` (so mid B=8 and large B=4 split; small B=2 and awkward B=1 keep the single-chunk path of step 4 untouched). Rationale: each chunk must keep full wave counts.
7. Two-stream path: `cur = torch.cuda.current_stream()`; after the weight transform record `ev0 = torch.cuda.Event(); ev0.record(cur)`. For k in (0,1): `s = _STREAMS[k]`; `s.wait_event(ev0)`; `with torch.cuda.stream(s):` call `_run_chunk` with `xc.narrow(0, k*Bc, Bc)` (contiguous view of a contiguous NCHW tensor) and `out.narrow(0, k*Bc*C*HW, Bc*C*HW)`; record `ev[k]` on `s`.
8. Allocator safety: before forking, call `out.record_stream(s)`, `w1l.record_stream(s)`, `w2l.record_stream(s)` for both streams (they are allocated on `cur` but consumed on side streams). Intermediates (`xl`, conv outputs) are allocated inside the `with torch.cuda.stream(s)` block, so they are already stream-associated.
9. Join: `cur.wait_event(ev[0])` and `cur.wait_event(ev[1])` before returning `out.view(B,C,H,W)`. No `.cpu()`, no device transfers, no `get_inputs` changes.
10. Verify all four shapes numerically (B=1 and B=2 must take the untouched path), then confirm the split path is faster on 8x256x64x128 and 4x256x256x256; if either regresses, tighten the gate to `B>=8`.
strategy.evidence: Amdahl split from nsys: conv 63.4% (7,159us/24) vs glue 36.6%. The two phases stress disjoint units: the conv moves only ~268MB per forward over ~596us (~0.45 TB/s, ~24% of the 1.84 TB/s measured peak) while being tensor-core bound, whereas the glue is DRAM-saturated and SM-idle — gn_silu_nhwc gpu__dram_throughput 82.87% vs sm__throughput 28.32%, gn_stats 72.80% vs 19.81%, nchw_to_nhwc 81.77% vs 41.57%, gn_silu_res 77.80% vs 47.77%. Section analysis for gn_silu_nhwc states verbatim: 'This workload is utilizing greater than 80.0% of the available compute or memory performance of this device. To further improve performance, work will likely need to be shifted from the most utilized to another unit' — with the pipeline serialized there is no other unit to shift to, which is exactly what two streams provide. Ruled out as #1: per-kernel coalescing/latency tuning. gn_silu_nhwc already runs at 82.87% DRAM with smsp__sass_branch_targets_threads_divergent.sum = 0, achieved occupancy 78.66% and float4 accesses; the glue's 603MB/forward costs 328us at 1.84 TB/s versus 345us measured, i.e. only ~5% of the glue is efficiency loss — so no coalescing/vector-width change can yield more than ~2% overall. History: Attempt #1 (fp16 conv1 path) is case (a) — the byte/precision lever was applied but the score moved -0.85% and the large shape -1.2%, so halving conv bytes is a dead end and I do not re-attempt precision changes. The REJECTED kernel_20260903_125102 profile shows the deciding defect of naive chunking: gn_stats launch__waves_per_multiprocessor fell to 0.75 (base 2.25) and its dram_throughput to 48.07% (base 72.80%) — it chunked into 4 pieces of B=2 with grid (8,64)=512 blocks. My concrete delta: 2 chunks, gated to B>=4, which keeps gn_stats at ~2048 blocks (S = ceil(2048/BG) with BG=128 or 64 still yields 2048 blocks, 2.25 waves) and the elementwise kernels at ~9 waves, plus explicit event-ordered two-stream overlap rather than serial chunk execution. It composes with every mechanism the base carries: the specialized C=256/CPG=8 shift-mask index math, stride-9 padded shared transpose and custom NCHW->NHWC/weight transforms are used verbatim inside each chunk.
strategy.expected_metric_change: End-to-end forward time down (target 941us -> 700-800us on 8x256x64x128; floor is max(conv ~596us, total DRAM 871MB/1.84TB/s = 473us)); effective per-forward serialized GPU time down while per-kernel gpu__dram_throughput of the glue kernels stays >=70% and gn_stats launch__waves_per_multiprocessor stays >=2.0 (the metric that exposed the rejected 4-way chunking at 0.75); sm__throughput during the overlapped window rises because conv blocks fill the schedulers while glue blocks wait on long_scoreboard. Anti-regression: kernel launches per forward rise from 10 to 19 — this is accounted for and is only permitted on B>=4 shapes where per-forward GPU time is >1ms, so CPU launch cost (<80us, fully async) cannot dominate; registers/shared per kernel are unchanged (no kernel body edits except removing an at::empty), so achieved occupancy must stay at 88-93% for gn_silu_res and >=78% for gn_silu_nhwc; the B=2 and B=1 shapes must take the untouched single-chunk path and their times must not move; numerics must stay inside max_atol 0.0027-0.003 on all four shapes. If the base mechanisms were lost the tell would be the specialized kernel names disappearing from the timeline or gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel's shared_mem_per_block changing from 5632 — neither may happen.
strategy.first_milestone: Step 4 — the `gn_silu_res_nchw_into` variant plus the single-chunk refactor compiles and matches the reference on all four shapes with performance unchanged.
